input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: The guard `all(arg.help is not None for arg in args)` is True when there are no Argument params, so the Positional arguments heading is now emitted even for commands that take no arguments.
- rationale: Trigger: any command or group with no Argument parameters. all() over an empty sequence returns True, so formatter.section(_("Positional arguments")) runs with an empty records list. The section heading is written with no entries beneath it. Previously, nothing was written when args was empty. Impact: every help page for a command without positional arguments shows a spurious empty "Positional arguments:" heading.
critique: The finding points to the same faulty guard, `all(...)` over the arguments' help attributes, and describes one of the label's failure paths: `all([])` is True, so an empty 'Positional arguments' heading is printed for commands with no arguments. It does not mention the mixed-help case, but it names the same faulty operation and the same mechanism.
